artworks.title: Eurotas and Lakedaimonia mosaic
artworks.description: Hatay Archaeology Museum (inv. 826): Eurotas faces the labelled personification of Lakedaimonia — the Spartan land that takes its name from Lacedaemon, son of Zeus and Taygete. Late Antique floor art keeps the king’s eponym alive as geography even when the mortal founder himself goes unpainted.

artworks.title: Genealogy of Taygete and Lacedaemon
artworks.description: A schematic Pleiad genealogy naming Taygete and her son Lacedaemon — the stem by which Sparta’s eponymous king enters the Atlas line. Classroom mythography rather than salon painting, it still marks the rare places where Lacedaemon is labelled as a person.

popCulture.title: Lacedaemon (mythology)
popCulture.description: Son of Zeus by the Pleiad Taygete; husband of Sparte — the king after whom Lacedaemon (Sparta’s land) is named.
